notes:
- Primary contact: Nathan Riley (VP Product) — "we cannot tolerate >5m outage per month for patient flows"
- Use-case: 24/7 patient triage + downstream clinician summarization; mix of chat (low latency) and batch summaries (throughput)
- Latency SLOs discussed: target p95 ≤ 150ms for single-turn chat (non-streaming), p99 ≤ 400ms for multi-turn session with KV cache hits
- Throughput/guarantees: require baseline sustained throughput 1000 chats/minute (approx 18 qps sustained, burst to 120 qps); SE recommends 8x A100-eq GPUs with continuous batching profile; propose burst pool of 2 GPUs for peak windows
- Reserved planning: want fixed GPU allocation on Dedicated with autoscale disabled; legal asks for explicit GPU-count guarantees and planned ramp schedule during first 90 days
- SLA asks from Grayhawk legal: 99.95% monthly uptime for customer-facing endpoints, 99.9% for internal admin APIs, service credits escalator (see commercial notes)
- Credit schedule proposed by AE:
  * <99.95% uptime: 10% monthly credit
  * <99.9% uptime: 25% monthly credit
  * <99.5% uptime: 50% monthly credit + ability to terminate after 2 consecutive months below threshold
  Grayhawk counter: wants 15% / 35% / 60% and accelerated remedy for clinical-impacting incidents
- Maintenance windows: Grayhawk requires maintenance outside of 03:00-22:00 local hospital time (US EST) for patient flows; prefer single 4-hour monthly window, no forced upgrades during peak clinical hours
- Support SLAs: Grayhawk requests P1 response ≤ 15 minutes (phone + Slack) and P1 resolution target 4 hours or runbook-defined rollback; P2 response ≤ 1 hour; P3 next-business-day. Redwood current standard: P1 30m response, P2 2h. This is a negotiation point.
